To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have studied the initial stage of the formation of InxGa(1−x)As nanostructures by molecular beam epitaxy growth.
the initial stage of island formation in InxGa1−xAs/GaAs (001) structures is characterized by a lateral composition modulation with a period of about 60 nm.
the initial stage of island formation in the InxGa1−xAs/GaAs system with low indium composition is accompanied by lateral ordering of the islands with a periodicity of about 50 nm.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the initial stages of the strain-driven island formation in InxGa1−xAs/GaAs heterostructures with low indium concentration (x = 0.20 to 0.35).
the growth and characterization of InxGaAs quantum dots (QD) on GaAs (001) substrates with low In content (x < 0.35) and with the study of their optical and structural properties.
the growth and characterization of InxGa(1-x)As/GaAs multilayer structures with x = 0, 20, 25, 30, 33 and 35% by molecular beam epitaxy (MBE).
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
for low indium content InxGa1−xAs/GaAs quantum dots, the formation of a vertical dot superlattice is not a necessary condition for the formation of quantum dot states.
the initial stage formation of quantum dots is a complex process, in which both the strain and composition modulation are involved.
the formation of the quantum dots in the InxGa1xAs/GaAs heterostructures is a complex process which involves a large number of parameters.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the formation of quantum dot superlattices with low indium composition can be controlled by changing the growth conditions, which leads to a change in the lateral composition modulation period.

the formation of InxGa(1-x)As/GaAs quantum dots with low In content is a complex process, which is governed by a number of factors, such as the thickness of the InxGa1- xAs layer, strain, and lateral composition modulation.
the formation of InxGa(1-x)As/GaAs islands in the early stage is accompanied by a lateral composition modulation with the period of about 60 nm.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the initial stage of formation of nanostructures in the InxGa1−xAs/GaAs system with low indium composition is accompanied by the formation of a lateral composition modulation (LCM) with a period of about 60 nm in the [110] direction.
the initial stage of island formation is accompanied by lateral composition modulation and the degree of vertical dot stacking is determined by the InxGa1−xAs layer thickness.
the lateral ordering of the dots is not the result of the strain relaxation but rather the result of the initial stage formation of the nanoislands.
